key_insight: Quantum circuits can avoid barren plateaus when input and observable structure align within a polynomial-dimensional invariant subspace that the differentiated gate moves sufficiently.
engineering_relevance: The framework can help assess circuit trainability before expensive optimization and guide ansatz design toward nonvanishing gradient variance.
method: Decompose the circuit’s compact Lie group representation to bound gradient variance for arbitrary inputs and observables.
Derive exact variance when circuit segments on both sides of the differentiated gate form 2-designs.
Estimate variance from ansatz runs without constructing representation-theoretic projectors.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical variance bounds, a sufficient trainability condition, and a sampling algorithm using polynomially many runs in inverse tolerance, but no empirical benchmarks.
watch_item: The trainability condition is sufficient, not necessary, and sampling costs may become large for very small variance tolerances.
